deliverables: Milestone-based disbursement controls through TRSC/PSSC smart contracts
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, submitted by Intersect on behalf of the vendor; vendor identified as Teragone in the funding disclosure.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Mithril Protocol continued development through the Intersect budget process.

claims.claim: Mithril uses stake-based threshold multi-signatures to certify Cardano state in a trustless way so nodes and applications can verify state rapidly without relying on the entire chain.
Full node synchronisation is slow today and light clients rely on centralized trust.
Funding Mithril continued development through Intersect MBO is presented as preserving Cardano decentralization while supporting scaling.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The requested 3,810,423 ada consists of 3,699,440 ada for Mithril Protocol Continuous Development and 110,983 ada for the Intersect Budget Administration fee.
The proposer states the withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit at the time of submission, either on its own or in aggregate.

Audit and oversight costs are included in the proposal overhead and administration fee, with independent oversight through Intersect and technically capable third parties plus reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.
Teragone has not previously received direct funding from Cardano treasury or community governance programs, while prior Mithril work was funded by IOG.
Intersect will use Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with one Treasury Reserve Smart Contract and one Project-Specific Smart Contract for administration and disbursement.

The Oversight Committee is stated to consist of Sundae Labs, Cardano Foundation, Dquadrant, NMKR, Sundial, and Eternl, and to verify key administrative actions using on-chain logic without discretion over governance decisions.

summary: The document requests 3,810,423 ada for Mithril Protocol continued development and Intersect administration, arguing that Mithril provides trustless rapid state verification, has budget-process approval, complies with the NCL at submission, and will be managed through smart-contract-based treasury controls with external oversight.
